acceptance_criteria.statement: When the service is failing in the ways it has failed before, a monitoring signal exposed by the service reports that failure without a customer having to report it first.
An observer can distinguish, from outside the service, a healthy service from one whose dependencies are unhealthy.
When a dependency the service relies on is unhealthy or unresponsive, the service continues to answer requests it can still serve rather than failing wholesale or amplifying the dependency's failure.
A customer can retrieve, in one request, analytics covering their links as a whole rather than a single link at a time.
The overall analytics response reflects clicks that have been made against the customer's links.
A customer can retrieve a breakdown of clicks by where the clicks came from.
The existing per-link click count and redirect behaviour continue to work unchanged.
No user interface is delivered; every new capability is reachable through the service's existing API and operational surfaces.

constraints: Java 21 and Spring Boot (existing service is Spring Boot 3.5)
PostgreSQL and Redis only — 'no new database technology'

Brownfield: an existing, deployed URL shortener with a published OpenAPI contract in artifacts/openapi.yaml, PostgreSQL as system of record and Redis for the resolution cache, click counters and rate-limit buckets
Stated as 'the next thing we want after the sign-up work' and 'the current priority'
'We would like it soon' — a stated urgency with no date attached
Three larger accounts have asked sales for the overall analytics; one of them asked about the origin breakdown
AMBIGUITY (recorded, not resolved): 'where the clicks came from' is undefined — could mean geography, referrer, device/user-agent or client IP
AMBIGUITY (recorded, not resolved): 'more reliable' is unquantified — no availability target, error budget or latency bound
AMBIGUITY (recorded, not resolved): 'cope better when things around it are unhealthy' does not name which surrounding systems, nor what 'we made it worse' meant in the last outage
AMBIGUITY (recorded, not resolved): 'we should know before they do' does not say what is alerted, to whom, or through what
AMBIGUITY (recorded, not resolved): 'how their links are performing overall' fixes no time window, granularity or metric set, and does not say whether 'overall' is per-customer or service-wide
AMBIGUITY (recorded, not resolved): whether the origin breakdown applies to the overall analytics, to per-link analytics, or both
AMBIGUITY (recorded, not resolved): 'soon' is an urgency with no date
output.goal: Make the existing URL shortener more reliable — so we detect its problems before customers report them and it degrades better when its dependencies are unhealthy — and give customers analytics across all of their links rather than one link at a time.
in_scope: Reliability work on the existing shortener service, treated as the higher priority of the two asks ('reliability first')
Being alerted to a failure ourselves before a customer tells us about it — the requirement's phrase is 'we should know before they do'
Coping better when surrounding/dependent systems are unhealthy, so that an outage originating elsewhere is not made worse by this service
Analytics that let a customer understand how their links are performing overall (aggregate across links), beyond the per-link numbers already reported
A breakdown of clicks by 'where the clicks came from', as asked for by one of the larger accounts
Delivery as the next piece of work after the sign-up work already completed
non_functional: Reliability: the service has fallen over twice this quarter; the ask is that recurrence is both less likely and self-detected
Observability/operability: failures must be visible to us through our own monitoring before customers notice
Resilience: degradation of an upstream or downstream dependency must not be amplified by this service
The click/redirect path is the most availability-sensitive surface and must not be made slower or more failure-prone by analytics collection
Analytics aggregated across a customer's links must remain responsive as link and click volume grows
Click-origin data is per-click information about end users, carrying privacy expectations the requirement does not state
out_of_scope: Any UI — explicitly excluded ('no UI in this build'); analytics are API-only
Introducing any new database or storage technology beyond PostgreSQL and Redis
Changes to the sign-up work, which is stated as already done and not part of this ask
Authentication and authorisation changes — the requirement says nothing about who may read the new analytics or about access control on them
Analytics for anonymous (unowned) links, which today have no owner and no readable click count; the requirement does not mention them
Data retention, deletion or privacy handling for any click-origin data — not mentioned in the requirement
Billing, quotas or pricing tiers for analytics, including for the three named larger accounts
Export, download, scheduled reporting or webhook delivery of analytics
Backfill or reconstruction of historical click-origin data for clicks already served
Multi-region, replica or failover deployment topology changes
A specific numeric availability target or SLA — none was stated
Changes to redirect semantics, link creation, expiry, abuse handling or the existing per-link click count
Choosing or standing up external monitoring/alerting infrastructure (paging, on-call routing) — the requirement asks only that we know first, and names no system

answers.Q1: The referring site: the Referer header reduced to a registrable domain, with absent or stripped referrers bucketed as 'direct'. No geolocation, no device parsing, no IP retention -- we do not want to take on a geo database or a privacy retention question in this change.
answers.Q2: Yes, and that is what happened. The platform routes on /actuator/health and the readiness probe includes Redis, so a Redis blip pulled every instance out of service at once -- that is what 'we made it worse' meant. Fix it: liveness depends on no external dependency, readiness depends on PostgreSQL only, and Redis is a non-gating indicator on a detail health group plus a Prometheus gauge.

payload.note: Answer set A. Reliability is probe surgery plus the alerting gap -- we should know before the customer does -- and explicitly not a resilience library. Analytics is a referrer rollup, aggregate over a window, near-real-time with the freshness field as proposed. Advisory answers Q3-Q8 accepted as proposed.

output.blast_radius: The dangerous half of this change is not the analytics endpoints, it is that both increments reach into the click path and the Redis keyspace the click path shares. GET /{code} is unauthenticated, is the highest-volume route in the service, and is written so that anything thrown inside it becomes a 404 rather than a 500 - so the worst plausible failure is not an error rate, it is silence: a bad origin derivation (a malformed, enormous or absent Referer) turns live links into 'not found' for every clicker, no 5xx appears on any dashboard, the click is not counted, and the first report comes from a customer whose campaign traffic evaporated. The second-worst is quieter still: origin counters sharing the clicks:pending hash would make the existing Lua flush ignore or delete fields, and the number a customer reads as clickCount - durable total plus un-flushed delta - would drift wrong in a direction nobody is alerted on, while every test that runs against a single fresh instance passes. The reliability half carries the mirror-image risk: it edits the meaning of /actuator/health, the signal the runbook tells operators to trust and which some platform outside this repository may be routing on, and it puts a breaker in front of the one Redis call deliberately allowed to fail a request, so a change intended to stop amplifying a dependency outage can lengthen the create outage instead. Everything else - a new table, two new owner-scoped read endpoints, an OpenAPI minor bump - is additive and would fail loudly. Review attention belongs on RedirectController, RedisClickCounter plus the Lua script, and the health-group configuration in application.yml; the analytics query and response shapes need a contract read, not a risk read.

breaking_changes.detail: Today the aggregate includes the auto-configured Redis indicator and reports DOWN while redirects are still being served - RUNBOOK.md:30 documents this URL as the health check and :137 records exactly that symptom. Making Redis non-gating changes the answer at an unchanged URL. Old and new pods run together during a rolling deploy, so for the length of the rollout the same probe against the same service gets DOWN from one pod and UP from the next; a platform that pulls or restarts on DOWN will do so to half the fleet.
breaking_changes.mitigation: Two phases. Phase 1 (this change): leave the aggregate's membership as it is, add a named detail group (e.g. /actuator/health/dependencies) and a Prometheus gauge per dependency, and confirm with whoever owns the deployment manifests - which live outside this repository, per Q2 - that the probe is repointed at /actuator/health/readiness, which today contains only readinessState and is already Redis-independent. Phase 2, after that confirmation lands: drop Redis from the aggregate. Update the RUNBOOK's health-check example and its failure-mode row in the same commit as each phase so the documented signal never disagrees with the service.

breaking_changes.detail: ResolutionCache.invalidateBeforeIssuing is the only 503 in the service and is per-request: each create makes its own attempt bounded by the 1s Lettuce timeout, so creates start succeeding the instant Redis recovers. A circuit breaker placed around the shared Redis client would keep refusing creates for the whole open window after recovery, lengthening a create outage the contract documents as deliberate - and an open breaker also suppresses the eviction that makes issuing a code safe.
breaking_changes.mitigation: Scope the breaker to the best-effort calls only - resolution reads/writes, click counting, rate-limit consumption - and never to invalidateBeforeIssuing, which keeps its own per-request attempt. If it must cover it, bound the open state well below app.cache.ttl (PT60S) and half-open on the first request, so the worst case is one extra refused create rather than a window of them.

breaking_changes.detail: read_click_deltas.lua HDELs any field of the pending hash whose value is 0, and RedisClickCounter.readPending discards any field that is not a UUID (logging 'Ignored N click delta(s) whose key was not a link id'). During a rolling deploy the old image runs that script against the same hash the new image is writing to. Origin fields written into clicks:pending would be dropped by old pods and would flood their logs; a zero-valued origin field would be deleted by an old pod mid-flight.
breaking_changes.mitigation: Give origin counters their own key namespace (e.g. clicks:origins:<yyyy-mm-dd>) that no existing script touches, leaving clicks:pending's field space UUID-only. Old pods then ignore the new keys entirely and the two versions coexist with no coordination. Ship the flush-side reader of the new key before or with the writer, never after.
breaking_changes.surface: Redis keyspace clicks:* shared between old and new pods

breaking_changes.detail: Old pods have no mapping for the new paths, so an authenticated caller gets a 404 - and since ApiExceptionHandler has no no-handler-found branch, Spring's default body rather than the declared ApiError shape. The RUNBOOK already records this exact pattern for the sign-up and anonymous-link rollout.
breaking_changes.mitigation: Announce the endpoints to the three named accounts only once the rollout reports complete, as the RUNBOOK's existing note prescribes; nothing in the code fixes it. Bump artifacts/openapi.yaml to 1.2.0 so a client can tell which contract it is talking to.
breaking_changes.surface: GET /api/v1/links/{code}/... and the new aggregate endpoint during rollout

breaking_changes.detail: Hibernate validates the mapped schema at startup, so a pod carrying the new rollup entity will not start against a database that has not had V5 applied - the RUNBOOK's 'service will not start' row is the symptom an operator sees. In the other direction, rollback to the previous image is safe only because the migration is additive.
breaking_changes.mitigation: Apply V5 ahead of the image that maps it, exactly as V4's own header spells out for the anonymous-links change; keep it additive-only so the previous image still validates; treat 'stop writing and let the retention purge drain' as the rollback rather than a down-migration.
breaking_changes.surface: Database schema vs running image (ddl-auto: validate)

impacted.notes: Origin derivation (A1/A4) lands on the only path that must never 5xx. It already wraps the whole handler in catch(RuntimeException) -> notFound(), so a derivation bug does not surface as a 500: it silently converts live 302s into 404s and stops counting the click. Referer is not read anywhere in this class today (only getRemoteAddr()); adding a header read plus a registrable-domain reduction adds per-click CPU inside the try block.

record()/pendingDelta()/readPending()/settle() all address one hash, properties.click().keyPrefix() + 'pending' (app.click.key-prefix=clicks:). Folding origin counters in here must not change that hash's field space - see the read_click_deltas.lua entry. Also the natural home for the Micrometer counters AC1 needs (clicks dropped, settle failures).

HGETALLs the pending hash, HDELs any field whose value is exactly 0, and returns the rest. RedisClickCounter.readPending then UUID.fromString()s every field and logs 'Ignored N click delta(s) whose key was not a link id' for the rest. Any origin field written into the same hash is therefore either ignored-with-a-warning or silently HDELed at zero. Origin counters must live under a separate key.

The only drain, @Scheduled(fixedDelayString=${app.click.flush-interval:PT5S}), read -> write -> settle. A4 reuses it for origin/rollup deltas, so the pass now has two failure domains but one loop; a per-entry RuntimeException already 'continue's, so a rollup write failure must not skip counter.settle() for the click delta or clicks get written twice. AC1's 'flush failing repeatedly' signal belongs here.
Writes the durable increment via LinkRepository.addClicks. Gains the daily-rollup / origin upsert in the same transaction; a failure here now costs both a click delta and an origin delta a retry.

Interface signature change (record(UUID) gains an origin argument, or a sibling method). Implemented by RedisClickCounter and injected into RedirectController and LinkService; its javadoc contract ('must never throw, must never delay the 302') is what the new argument has to keep.

toResponse() computes clickCount as durable + clickCounter.pendingDelta(link.getId()). It is not edited, but AC7's 'unchanged' depends entirely on the pending-hash layout and on pendingDelta still returning 0-on-failure. create() also calls resolutionCache.invalidateBeforeIssuing(), the one call that throws 503 - a circuit breaker around Redis changes when that fires.

Reads/invalidations already swallow failures; invalidateBeforeIssuing is the single source of 503 service_unavailable on create. If the A1 breaker wraps the shared Redis rather than only the best-effort calls, an open breaker turns create into a fast, sustained 503 for the whole open window instead of a per-request 1s attempt.

Documented to fail open on any RuntimeException. A breaker in front changes only the latency of failing open (1s timeout per bucket call vs immediate), which is a genuine improvement on the click path - it consumes two buckets per 404 - but it also means an open breaker unmeters sign-up and anonymous-create for its whole window, the gap the RUNBOOK already flags.

No HealthIndicator and no MeterRegistry injection exists anywhere in service/src/main today - grep returns nothing. AC1/AC2 are entirely new code: a Redis indicator bound to a named health group, a flush-staleness indicator, and Prometheus gauges. Nothing on the classpath is missing (spring-boot-starter-actuator at pom.xml:64, micrometer-registry-prometheus at :179).

application.yml sets probes.enabled + show-details: when-authorized and configures no health groups, so Boot's defaults apply today: /actuator/health/readiness contains only readinessState (Redis does not affect it) while the aggregate /actuator/health includes the auto-configured redis and db indicators and goes DOWN on a Redis blip. RUNBOOK.md:30 documents a request to /actuator/health as the health check and RUNBOOK.md:137 records 'health DOWN, redirects still working'. Whatever AC2/AC3 change here changes what an existing external prober sees.

Protected path (orchestrator/pipelines/sdlc.yaml:56). Needs management.endpoint.health.group.* for the detail group, plus app.analytics.* (window cap, top-N, retention). Every new key must be mirrored in AppProperties or binding fails at startup.

@ConfigurationProperties record described in its own javadoc as part of the frozen contract; gains an Analytics nested record. Constructor binding means a mismatch with application.yml is a context-load failure across the whole integration suite, not a single test failure.

Protected path; ddl-auto: validate, so the migration must be applied before any pod maps the new entity or startup fails outright (RUNBOOK: 'Everything 5xx / service will not start'). Additive only per A12 - links and its ix_links_owner_listing index are untouched, which is what keeps AC7 mechanically true.

New JPA entity + repository for the (link, origin, UTC day) counters. The aggregate query must be owner-scoped by joining links.customer_id, which is how anonymous links (NULL since V4) are excluded by SQL equality rather than by a remembered filter.

Gains a count/aggregate finder for the customer-wide figures. Existing finders (findByDomainAndCode, findByDomainAndCodeAndCustomerId, findOwnedBy, addClicks) are read by the redirect, management and flush paths and must not be touched.

WebConfig registers SessionAuthenticationFilter for the servlet pattern /api/v1/* only, and shouldNotFilter exempts three paths by exact equality, so new sub-resources inherit bearer auth with no config change. Paging/window validation must reproduce LinkController.requireValidPaging exactly: refuse rather than clamp, 400 invalid_request with a field map.

New records only. LinkResponse must not change (AC7); note its javadoc currently asserts clickCount is 'the whole of how a link has performed... No time series, referrer, geography', which becomes stale prose the moment the new endpoints exist.

The frozen contract (1.1.0) that the test authors work from in isolation. Adding paths under /api/v1/links takes it to 1.2.0 additively; the closed error catalogue in ErrorCode must gain no new value (A9), and the not_found body stays byte-identical.

Today: HINCRBY on click -> flush reads non-destructively -> addClicks -> settle subtracts; read path is durable + pendingDelta. The new rollup becomes a second reader of the same click event and a second writer in the same flush transaction. The invariant 'durable total + pending delta = clicks recorded' is what every per-link figure rests on and now has to survive a second write in the same pass.

Operational surface, not decoration: the health table (lines 115-130) and the failure-mode table (137-145) describe the exact behaviour AC2/AC3 change, and A7 puts the recommended alert expressions here. The row '/actuator/health DOWN, redirects still working' is the documented signal an operator may already be routing on.
Client-facing companion to the OpenAPI document; gains the two analytics endpoints or goes stale against 1.2.0.

Existing green tests that pin the behaviour this change moves under: exact click counts, count survival across restart, and the paused-Redis degradation contract (TestInfrastructure.resumeCounterTier). They are the mechanical detector for an AC7 regression and must keep passing untouched.

regression_surface: GET /{code} on a live link still answers 302 with Location byte-identical to the submitted longUrl and Cache-Control/Pragma/Expires unchanged, when Referer is absent, empty, malformed, an IP literal, an IDN, or maximum-length - the origin derivation must not be able to reach the catch block that turns a redirect into a 404.
GET /{code} still never returns 5xx, including when origin derivation or the origin write throws, and still answers the byte-identical not_found body for unissued, expired, deleted and blocked codes.

clickCount after N served clicks equals N exactly and immediately (durable total + pendingDelta), not one flush behind - ClickCountingTest and LinkPerformanceTest pin this and it is the AC7 tripwire for any change to the clicks:pending hash layout.

Click deltas survive a flush that fails part-way and a restart: the read stays non-destructive, settle subtracts exactly what was written, and a negative pending field still flushes like any other delta (DurabilityAcrossRestartTest).

With Redis paused: 302 still served from PostgreSQL, rate limiting still fails open, create still 503s, and the new analytics endpoints answer 200 with durable figures and a freshness marker rather than 503 (DegradedDependencyTest is the harness).
The click bucket and the not-found bucket stay separate and 429 still carries Retry-After >= 1 - a breaker in front of the limiter must not collapse them or emit Retry-After: 0.
New analytics endpoints sit inside the session filter: absent, malformed and expired tokens all give the same 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer, since shouldNotFilter exempts only three exact paths.
Analytics never include another customer's links and never include anonymous links (customer_id NULL since V4) - owner scoping in the query, not a post-fetch filter.
Paging and window parameters on the new endpoints refuse rather than clamp, with 400 invalid_request and a field map, matching LinkController's 0-based page and 1..100 size.

/actuator/health, /actuator/health/liveness and /actuator/health/readiness status codes and payloads, including that show-details: when-authorized still hides per-dependency detail from an unauthenticated caller on the aggregate.
Application startup against a migrated database with ddl-auto: validate, and startup with the new app.analytics.* keys bound through AppProperties.
Reserved alias refusal still returns 400 invalid_request for actuator/health/metrics/prometheus/api, so no customer link can shadow the new operational or analytics routes.
The flush scheduler still drains within app.click.flush-interval under load while also writing rollup rows - a slower pass is the failure mode that makes clickCount lag and the rollup stale at once.

evidence.claim: No public-suffix-list implementation is available to main code: service/pom.xml declares no Guava, no Apache HttpClient, no PSL artifact. The only httpclient5 in the local repository arrives through test-scoped testcontainers/docker-java. Registrable-domain reduction therefore cannot be done correctly without the new dependency A1 forbids.
evidence.source: service/pom.xml:49-207 (full dependency list); ls ~/.m2/repository/com/google -> only 'code', 'errorprone' (no guava); find ~/.m2 -iname '*publicsuffix*' -> no matches

evidence.claim: A reusable, fail-closed host canonicaliser already exists and is public: HostNormalizer.normalize() strips trailing dots, lower-cases with Locale.ROOT, applies IDN.toASCII, rejects empty labels and canonicalises numeric IPv4, returning Optional.empty() instead of throwing on anything ambiguous. It stops short of eTLD+1.

The redirect handler wraps everything in catch(RuntimeException) -> notFound(), so any exception from a new origin derivation converts a live 302 into a 404 with no 5xx and no counted click - the silent failure mode the impact analysis names. It reads only getRemoteAddr() today; Referer appears nowhere in src.

The click path makes exactly three Redis round trips on a cache hit - the rate-limit Lua script, the resolution-cache get, and the HINCRBY - each bounded by the 1s Lettuce command/connect timeout. An additional origin write is a fourth unless folded into one script.
evidence.source: RedirectController.java:66,71,73 -> RedisTokenBucketRateLimiter.consume (one script execute), LinkResolver.resolve -> ResolutionCache.get, RedisClickCounter.record; application.yml:90-95 ('the click path talks to Redis three times', timeout: 1s)

evidence.claim: Only one Redis key is touched by the counter and its Lua script: pendingKey = app.click.key-prefix + 'pending' ('clicks:pending'). read_click_deltas.lua HGETALLs that key, HDELs any field whose value is exactly 0, and readPending discards non-UUID fields with a WARN. An origin counter under a different key (e.g. clicks:origins:<date>) is invisible to old pods, so the rolling-deploy coexistence mitigation is sound.

ClickFlushWriter.write is a single @Transactional per link containing only links.addClicks. Putting the rollup upsert in that same transaction couples them: a rollup failure rolls back the durable click write too, so the delta stays pending and is retried (no double count, AC7 preserved), but a permanently failing rollup row would block that link's durable click writes indefinitely.
evidence.source: service/src/main/java/com/example/urlshortener/click/ClickFlushWriter.java:277-285; ClickFlushJob.flush loop at ClickFlushJob.java:225-243 (settle only after a successful write)

evidence.claim: Spring Boot's built-in probe groups are liveness -> livenessState and readiness -> readinessState, with additional paths /livez and /readyz. No dependency indicator is in either today, so the readiness probe is already Redis-independent and Postgres-independent.

The Redis health indicator is auto-configured (RedisHealthContributorAutoConfiguration is on the classpath), which is why the aggregate /actuator/health goes DOWN on a Redis blip while redirects keep working - exactly as the runbook records.

A named health group can set its own show-details, but the field is nullable and inherits the endpoint-level 'when-authorized' when unset. With no Spring Security filter chain in this service, 'authorized' is never satisfied, so a detail group without an explicit show-details: always would return only {"status":"UP"} and would not satisfy AC2.
evidence.source: javap -p HealthEndpointProperties$Group.class (fields: include, exclude, showDetails, additionalPath); application.yml:115-119 (show-details: when-authorized); service/pom.xml:119-122 (spring-security-crypto only, deliberately no starter-security)

evidence.claim: Actuator is served on the application's public port: application.yml sets server.port 8080 and no management.server.port, and /actuator/metrics and /actuator/prometheus are already in the exposure list. A8's 'reachable only from inside the deployment network' rests entirely on an ingress rule that does not exist in this repository.
evidence.source: service/src/main/resources/application.yml:104-119; docs/RUNBOOK.md:30 (curl http://localhost:8080/actuator/health), :117-118 ('Actuator is outside the authentication filter ... and is unauthenticated')

evidence.claim: No HealthIndicator and no MeterRegistry injection exists anywhere in the service source, so AC1/AC2 are wholly new code - but nothing is missing from the build: spring-boot-starter-actuator (compile) brings micrometer-core and micrometer-registry-prometheus is declared at runtime scope.
evidence.source: grep -rn -e MeterRegistry -e HealthIndicator -e micrometer service/src --include='*.java' -> no matches; service/pom.xml:62-65,178-182; ls ~/.m2/repository/io/micrometer -> micrometer-core present

evidence.claim: New query parameters on the analytics endpoints are already covered by the frozen error shape: MethodArgumentTypeMismatchException maps to 400 invalid_request with {name: 'is not valid'} and MissingServletRequestParameterException to {name: 'is required'}, both through the same ApiError body. No new handler and no new error code is needed for window/paging parsing.
Paging validation to copy is exact and refuses rather than clamps: page < 0 -> {'page':'must not be negative'}, size outside 1..100 -> {'size':'must be between 1 and 100'}.

The session filter is registered as a servlet prefix mapping /api/v1/*, so any new sub-path under it is authenticated with no config change; exemptions are exact-equality on three literal paths (/api/v1/sessions, /api/v1/customers, /api/v1/public/links) and cannot leak to a new endpoint.

A customer-wide aggregate mounted at /api/v1/links/analytics would shadow GET /api/v1/links/{code} for a link whose code is 'analytics': the alias charset permits it and RESERVED_CODES does not list 'analytics', 'stats' or 'origins' (it lists api, actuator, health, info, metrics, prometheus, links, ...). The per-link sub-resource /api/v1/links/{code}/origins has no such conflict.

Owner scoping for the aggregate is mechanical rather than remembered: customer_id became nullable in V4 for anonymous links, and every owner-scoped query is an SQL equality on customer_id, which never matches NULL. The existing index ix_links_owner_listing (customer_id, created_at DESC, code ASC) already serves a customer_id equality predicate, so a rollup joined to links on customer_id needs no new index on links.

The degradation harness needed for A6's 'analytics answer 200 with a freshness marker while Redis is down' already exists and is reversible: TestInfrastructure pauses the Redis container with docker pause (keeping the port mapping) and DegradedDependencyTest resumes it in @AfterEach.

invalidateBeforeIssuing is the only 503 in the service and is a single cache.evict per create, so creates recover the instant Redis does - confirming the impact analysis's warning that a breaker covering it would extend a create outage past recovery. Every other cache operation already swallows RuntimeException.

LinkResponse's javadoc explicitly asserts the click count is the only figure and that time series, referrer, geography, device and unique-visitor data are out of scope; it becomes stale prose the moment these endpoints exist, and it sits in a file AC7 says must not change shape.

No maximum HTTP request header size is configured, so Boot's default applies and an oversized Referer is refused by the container before it reaches the handler; the derivation still has to survive an empty, malformed or non-URL Referer, which is a string it must never parse with anything that throws uncaught.
evidence.source: service/src/main/resources/application.yml:104-108 (server block: port and error settings only, no max-http-request-header-size)

evidence.claim: The working tree carries no uncommitted source changes; the last three commits are intake, clarify and impact-analysis only, so nothing has been implemented ahead of this spike.
evidence.source: git status --porcelain (only untracked service/.claude/, service/.mcp.json); git log --oneline -3

options.summary: Origin value = canonicalised Referer host via the existing HostNormalizer, no eTLD+1 reduction ('blog.example.co.uk' stored as-is), absent/unparseable -> 'direct'. No new dependency; reduction to a registrable domain remains possible later in the read query or a follow-up migration.

Approximate the registrable domain by keeping the last two labels of the host. No dependency, but wrong for every multi-label public suffix ('blog.example.co.uk' -> 'co.uk', 'x.github.io' -> 'github.io'), and with no backfill the wrong grouping is permanent in stored rows.

Add a public-suffix-list dependency (e.g. Guava or a standalone PSL library) to service/pom.xml so the registrable domain is computed correctly. Contradicts A1, touches a protected path, and forces a supply-chain approval that blocks the parallel implement/author-tests branches until a human rules.

unknowns.current_best_answer: Store the canonicalised host produced by the existing HostNormalizer (lower-cased, trailing dots stripped, IDN->ASCII, IPv4 literals canonicalised), with absent/empty/unparseable Referer bucketed as 'direct'. No PSL reduction; group by host.
unknowns.how_to_settle: One reviewer sentence: 'full host is fine' or 'registrable domain is required, add the PSL dependency to pom.xml at the design approval gate'. Confirm no PSL is present with: grep -n 'guava\|httpclient\|publicsuffix' service/pom.xml (returns nothing today).
unknowns.question: With no public-suffix list available (A1 forbids a new dependency), is it acceptable to store the canonicalised *host* of the Referer (e.g. `blog.example.co.uk`) rather than the registrable domain (`example.co.uk`)?
unknowns.why_it_matters: Nothing on the classpath can compute eTLD+1: service/pom.xml declares no Guava/httpclient/PSL artifact and HostNormalizer stops at canonicalisation. The naive substitute (keep the last two labels) is wrong for every multi-label suffix - `blog.example.co.uk` becomes `co.uk`, `x.github.io` becomes `github.io` - and A3 says there is no backfill, so a wrong reduction is baked into every row written before it is noticed and can never be recomputed. Full host is strictly more information and can be reduced later; a reduction cannot be undone.

unknowns.current_best_answer: Cap distinct origins per (link, day) at a configurable N (propose 50, app.analytics.max-origins-per-link-day); the N+1th and beyond increment a single 'other' field. Same value bounds storage and the response.
unknowns.how_to_settle: Reviewer sets a number, or design fixes one and states it. Cheap check on scale: the top-N the response already caps (A10) means anything beyond N is only ever read as 'other', so the storage cap can equal the response cap.
unknowns.question: What is the cap on distinct origin values per link per day, and what should overflow be called - is 50 with an 'other' bucket right?
unknowns.why_it_matters: Referer is attacker-controlled on an unauthenticated route (RedirectController:63 has no auth) and the click bucket allows 3000/min/IP. Without a cardinality cap, one sweep mints unbounded fields in the origin Redis key and unbounded rollup rows per link per day: the flush batch (app.click.flush-batch-size=500) starves behind junk, the daily rollup table grows without bound, and A11's 90-day retention only delays it. A cap is cheap to build in now and expensive to retro-fit once rows exist (no backfill, no recompute).

unknowns.current_best_answer: Assume the ingress does not filter it (nothing in this repo does), so the detail group must be treated as public: set show-details: always on the dependencies group only if the reviewer accepts that, otherwise carry AC2's detail purely on Prometheus gauges, which are already exposed on the same terms.
unknowns.how_to_settle: Ask whoever owns the ingress/deployment manifests (they live outside this repo, per Q2), or curl the public hostname: `curl -s https://<public-host>/actuator/prometheus | head`. Note /actuator/prometheus and /actuator/metrics are already in the exposure list (application.yml:114), so if that returns data the exposure question is already answered in the affirmative for the existing build.
unknowns.question: Is `/actuator/**` blocked at the ingress, or is it reachable from the public internet on the same host that serves redirects?
unknowns.why_it_matters: There is no management.server.port in application.yml, so actuator shares server.port 8080 with the public redirect (RUNBOOK.md:30 curls http://localhost:8080/actuator/health). A8 assumes the management surface is internal-only, and AC2's per-dependency detail depends on it: a named health group inherits show-details: when-authorized unless the group sets show-details, and with no Spring Security filter chain 'authorized' is never true - so the group either shows nothing useful or must be set to `always`, which publishes 'redis is DOWN' to whoever asks. Getting this wrong is a security posture change on a protected file.

unknowns.current_best_answer: Put the aggregate at /api/v1/analytics (still inside the session filter - WebConfig registers /api/v1/* as a servlet prefix mapping, so every sub-path is covered) and leave /api/v1/links/{code}/origins as the per-link sub-resource.
unknowns.how_to_settle: Design picks the path. To check the live namespace: `SELECT code FROM links WHERE lower(code) IN ('analytics','stats','origins');` - a non-empty result makes the collision real rather than theoretical.
unknowns.question: Where should the customer-wide aggregate endpoint live - `/api/v1/analytics/...` rather than `/api/v1/links/analytics`? And does any existing link already have the code `analytics`?
unknowns.why_it_matters: `GET /api/v1/links/{code}` exists (LinkController:77) and AliasPolicy.RESERVED_CODES does not contain 'analytics', 'stats' or 'origins', while the alias pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{3,64}$ permits all three. A literal path under /api/v1/links/ wins over the template in Spring MVC, so an existing customer's link with that code becomes unreadable through the API with no error anywhere. Moving the aggregate one segment up removes the class of bug entirely and costs nothing; the per-link sub-resource /api/v1/links/{code}/origins has no such problem.

unknowns.current_best_answer: One Lua script per click writing both the pending-hash field and the origin field, so the round-trip count stays at three and the origin write cannot fail independently of the click write.
unknowns.how_to_settle: Design decides; it is a code-shape choice, not a product one. Measurable afterwards with the existing harness: DegradedDependencyTest pauses the Redis container (TestInfrastructure.pauseCounterTier, docker pause) and asserts a click is still served - time that request before and after.
unknowns.question: May the click path make a 4th Redis round trip, or must the link counter and the origin counter be incremented in one call (a single Lua script)?
unknowns.why_it_matters: application.yml:90-95 states the click path talks to Redis three times, and the code confirms it: rate-limit script, cache get, HINCRBY. Each is bounded by the 1s Lettuce command timeout, so a Redis brownout costs up to ~3s per click today. A separate HINCRBY for the origin makes it four and raises the worst case by a third, on the route the whole reliability half of this change exists to protect. One script that increments both fields keeps the count at three.

unknowns.current_best_answer: Keep the readiness group as readinessState only for this increment and surface db and redis on the non-gating detail group plus Prometheus gauges; revisit once the probe's behaviour on failure is known.
unknowns.how_to_settle: One sentence from whoever owns the deployment manifests: does the readiness probe cause restarts, or only removal from the load-balancer pool? Removal-only makes db-in-readiness harmless (a pod with no database serves nothing anyway); restart-on-failure makes it a crash loop across the fleet during a failover.
unknowns.question: Should the readiness group actually include the PostgreSQL indicator, given every pod shares one database and would therefore go NOT_READY together?
unknowns.why_it_matters: Boot's built-in groups today are liveness->livenessState and readiness->readinessState (verified in AvailabilityProbesHealthEndpointGroups bytecode), so no dependency currently affects either probe. Adding db to readiness makes a database blip pull or restart the entire fleet at once - the same amplification shape the Redis change is being made to remove, just moved to the other dependency. It is worth a conscious decision rather than falling out of a config line.

payload.detail: all 8 acceptance criterion/a covered by the plan

risks: Q1 (blocking) has no recorded human answer, and the clarification's proposed answer — the Referer reduced to a registrable domain — is not buildable: feasibility evidence shows no public-suffix list on the classpath and A1 forbids adding one. T7 therefore stores the canonicalised full host per feasibility's recommended option (U1). Because A3 rules out backfill, this choice is permanent for every row written before it is revisited. A reviewer must confirm 'full host is fine' or approve a PSL dependency at the design gate.

Q2 (blocking) has no recorded human answer. The plan takes only phase 1 of the impact analysis's mitigation: the aggregate /actuator/health keeps its current membership and Redis stays gating on it. If some platform outside this repository is routing on that aggregate, the service continues to amplify a Redis blip into a fleet-wide outage — i.e. AC3 remains partially unmet by design until whoever owns the deployment manifests confirms the probe is repointed at /actuator/health/readiness. U6 (whether readiness should include PostgreSQL) is unresolved for the same reason and is deliberately not acted on.

T3 depends on U3: with no Spring Security filter chain, a health group inherits show-details: when-authorized and 'authorized' is never satisfied, so the dependencies group must be set to show-details: always to satisfy AC2. Actuator shares the public port 8080 and no ingress rule exists in this repository, so as planned this publishes 'redis is DOWN' to any caller. A8's internal-only assumption is unverified and is the load-bearing part of AC2's design.

T7/T8 sit inside RedirectController's catch(RuntimeException) -> notFound() block: a derivation or counter defect converts live 302s into 404s with no 5xx on any dashboard and no counted click. This failure is invisible to error-rate monitoring and would first surface as a customer reporting vanished campaign traffic.

T8's origin keyspace must stay disjoint from clicks:pending. If origin fields land in that hash, old pods running read_click_deltas.lua during a rolling deploy HDEL zero-valued fields and discard non-UUID fields with a WARN, corrupting the durable+pending invariant that AC7's clickCount rests on — and single-instance tests would all pass.

T4's breaker must not cover ResolutionCache.invalidateBeforeIssuing, the service's only deliberate 503. A breaker there keeps refusing creates for the whole open window after Redis recovers, lengthening an outage the change exists to shorten, and suppresses the eviction that makes issuing a code safe.

T9 puts a second writer in the flush transaction. A rollup row that fails permanently rolls back links.addClicks for that link, so its delta stays pending forever and its clickCount silently stops advancing; conversely a rollup failure that skips counter.settle() double-counts clicks. Both are AC7 regressions with no external error signal.
T6's V5 migration must be applied before any pod maps the new entity: ddl-auto is validate, so an image deployed ahead of the migration fails to start outright rather than degrading.

T8's distinct-origin cap is the only defence against attacker-controlled cardinality: Referer is unvalidated on an unauthenticated route with a 3000/min/IP bucket, so without the cap one sweep mints unbounded Redis fields and rollup rows, starving the 500-entry flush batch. U2 fixes no number; the plan assumes the storage cap equals the response top-N.

T11 mounts the customer-wide aggregate at /api/v1/analytics rather than /api/v1/links/analytics because a literal path under /api/v1/links/ would shadow GET /api/v1/links/{code} for any existing link whose code is 'analytics' — permitted by the alias charset and absent from RESERVED_CODES. If design moves it back under /api/v1/links, that collision returns silently.

The two increments are planned as independently deployable (A13), but T2 and T4 both edit RedisClickCounter and ResolutionCache while T8 and T9 edit the same click and flush classes. Landing them out of order, or in one release, concentrates unrelated risk on the highest-volume path.
